title: Lightning Seen from the ISS
kindLabel: No legend units: detected flashes are the data
sourceLabel: LIS on the International Space Station
description: Lightning events detected by the Lightning Imaging Sensor on the International Space Station, shown as a 10-day window rolling through the seasons. Every new flash becomes a percussive hit: left to right follows longitude, higher notes are further north. Listen to the storms swing between the hemispheres.
caveats: No colorbar or units: a flash is a detected event, and density is relative.
The Science On a Sphere movie has no date label, so this track describes seasons by where lightning is, not by calendar date.
90-second excerpt (source seconds 8 to 98) of a 100-second movie covering January 2017 to July 2023.
LIS on the ISS only sees between about 55 degrees north and south.
